title: Session-affine shadow bridge with graceful drift recovery and cohort quarantine lanes
author: Sana Patel
description: Motivation: We observed a class of subtle regressions that only surface for long-lived session flows (chat sessions with multi-turn state) when mirrored traffic is processed out-of-order or routed to different model variants during shadowing. This PR introduces a "session-affine shadow bridge" that preserves per-session routing affinity across the shadow path, a quarantine lane for cohorts that show drift, and a lightweight drift-recovery heuristic that can roll cohorts back gracefully without causing user-facing disruptions. Implementation summary: 1) bridge controller: new orchestrator component that binds session IDs to shadow lanes and ensures KV-cache affinity when shadow requests are forwarded; 2) cohort scoring: runtime hook that computes drift score from latency, top-k token divergence, and log-prob delta; 3) quarantine lane: an isolated path for cohorts with elevated drift where traffic is sampled for deep inspection and optional replay; 4) rollback heuristic: a time-windowed exponential backoff that reduces shadow weight and optionally triggers a supervised rollback for the canonical path; 5) telemetry: new metrics and tracing spans (session.bridge.assign, cohort.drift_score, quarantine.enter/exit) plus dashboard runbook. Backwards compatibility & safety: the bridge is opt-in via rollout config and defaults to pass-through for sessions without an ID. All changes are gated behind feature flags and include canary checks. Testing & validation: local integration harness runs mirrored and canonical paths with deterministic RNG to verify KV cache hits are preserved; synthetic long-session tests exercise drift scenarios; end-to-end load test validated p99 latency impact (<2% on a 1M RPS sample) and no KV cache eviction regressions. Rollout plan: staged rollout using existing orchestration: 0.1% -> 1% -> 10% -> 100% with cohort quarantine enabled at the 1% stage. Linear items: ENG-1428 implement bridge controller, ENG-1499 add cohort scoring and quarantine lanes. Related: incident INT-5083 (observed chat session divergence).
